Subject: Help: Apply calculated detection function to a different data set
Date: Wed, 4 Oct 2017 14:23:35 +0200
From: Ana Maria Prieto Ramirez <ana-maria.pr...@ufz.de>
To: dist...@st-andrews.ac.uk


Dear Distance team,

my name is Ana and I am PhD student at the Center for Environmental Research UFZ- Leipzig.
I am working with lizards' populations in fragmented landscapes, and applying distance sampling to calculate abundances.

My dataset is composed by  habitat patches, transects into each patch,  length of each transect, perpendicular distances of data points (lizards) to the transect, and in most cases
also an index of vegetation structure (IVS) derived from microhabitat data taken in plots around data points. So, the majority of my data points have a value for the IVS, but not all.

My approach is to generate a global detection function, and estimate abundances per habitat patch. I am applying a MCDS model, with IVS as covariate for detection. For the detection function I can obviously only use the
data points with a IVS value. On the other side, for the abundance estimate, i could use all my data points, given all of them have transect length and perpendicular distance to transect values. However, in the programm
detection function and abundance estimates are calculated in the same RUN. Therefore I would like to know if there is any way how to decouple the calculation of the detection function and the abundance estimate.
I mean, is it possible to generate the detection function with the dataset that has IVS,  and then apply it to the entire dataset for estimating abundance?


Thank you very much for your help in advance.
Best regards,
Ana


Ana María Prieto Ramírez
PhD student
Departement of Conservation Biology
Center for Environmental Research UFZ, Leipzig

messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Fwd: Help: Apply calculated detection function to a different data set
parts:
Ana

I think you would first want to establish whether the influence of your vegetation covariate is very strong.  You can establish that by setting a filter to exclude observations without the covariate; fit models with and without the covariate to determine if the covariate is meaningful.  Recognise also, in contrast to mark-recapture estimation, distance sampling is robust to unmodelled heterogeneity (called pooling robustness--see Section 11.12 of Advanced Distance Sampling by Buckland et al. (2004).

If you have established that you wish to conduct the hybrid analysis you describe in your question, then you could consider using the mark-recapture distance sampling engine (MRDS) for your analysis; described in Chapter 10 of the Distance 7.1 users guide.  In that chapter there is a description of how to organise your data as well as a section entitled "Using a previously fitted detection function to estimate density in MRDS".  This section addresses you situation.

Ana
